title: Adverbs
description: Learn adverbs for Grade 6: adverbs of manner, place, time, frequency and degree, how they are formed, their position and comparison — with bilingual notes, practice and tests.

topics.title: Kinds of Adverbs
topics.concept:
Adverbs are grouped by the question they answer.

  • Manner (how): quickly, bravely, well — She danced gracefully.
  • Place (where): here, there, above, outside — Wait outside.
  • Time (when): now, then, soon, yesterday — We will leave soon.
  • Frequency (how often): always, usually, often, sometimes, never — He never lies.
  • Degree (to what extent): very, quite, too, almost — It is too hot.

An adverb can describe a verb (run fast), an adjective (very tall) or another adverb (quite slowly).

examples.problem: Name the kind: She rarely watches TV.
examples.solution: Adverb of frequency — 'rarely' tells how often she watches TV.

examples.problem: Find the adverb of degree: The tea is too sweet.
examples.solution: too — it tells to what degree the tea is sweet.

recap: Adverbs answer how, where, when, how often, how much
Five kinds: manner, place, time, frequency, degree
Adverbs can modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs

topics.title: Forming Adverbs & Their Position
topics.concept:
Most adverbs of manner are made by adding -ly to an adjective:

  • quick → quickly, careful → carefully
  • happy → happily (y → i), gentle → gently (drop -e of -le)

But beware: fast, hard, late, early are the same as adjective and adverb (he runs fast). And good (adjective) becomes well (adverb).

Position

  • Manner adverbs usually go after the verb/object: She sang the song sweetly.
  • Frequency adverbs go before the main verb but after 'be': He always comes late; she is always happy.

examples.problem: Adjective or adverb? He is a good singer. He sings ___.
examples.solution: well — the adverb of 'good' is the irregular form 'well'.

recap: Some words (fast, hard, late) are both adjective and adverb
Frequency adverbs go before the main verb, but after 'be'

questions.explanation: 'never' fits before the past participle in a present perfect statement.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: He behaves in a friendly manner.
questions.explanation: 'friendly' is an adjective, not an adverb; use 'in a friendly manner'.

questions.q: Identify the error: 'She solved the puzzle more quicker than I did.'
Fill in: 'Hardly ___ he arrived when the bell rang.'
questions.explanation: After the negative adverb 'Hardly', use inversion with 'had': 'Hardly had he arrived'.

questions.q: Which adverb correctly modifies an adjective here? 'The film was ___ boring.'
questions.explanation: 'rather' is an adverb of degree modifying the adjective 'boring'.

questions.explanation: Front a negative adverb and invert: 'Rarely have I seen so beautiful a scene.'

questions.q: Choose the correct option: 'He works ___ hard, so he ___ fails.'
questions.explanation: 'very hard' (degree + adverb) and 'hardly ever' (almost never) fit the meaning.

intro.en: An adverb adds meaning to a verb, an adjective, or another adverb. It usually answers how, where, when, how often, or to what degree. In "She sings beautifully," the adverb beautifully tells us how she sings.
intro.hi: क्रिया-विशेषण (Adverb) क्रिया, विशेषण या किसी अन्य क्रिया-विशेषण की विशेषता बताता है। यह प्रायः बताता है कि काम कैसे, कहाँ, कब, कितनी बार या किस हद तक होता है। "She sings beautifully" में beautifully बताता है कि वह कैसे गाती है।

real_life.situation:
Your teacher gives feedback:

Teacher: You wrote the answer neatly and finished early. You always work very hard.
real_life.why: Each highlighted word is an adverb: neatly (how), early (when), always (how often), very (to what degree). One sentence, four kinds of adverb.

writing.prompt: Write five sentences about your school day, using an adverb of manner, time, frequency and degree.
writing.example: I always wake up early. I quickly get ready. The bus is usually very crowded.

micro_quiz.q: The adverb in 'He ran quickly' is:
micro_quiz.explanation: 'quickly' tells how he ran — adverb of manner.

micro_quiz.q: 'She is ___ kind.' Which adverb of degree fits?
micro_quiz.explanation: 'very' is an adverb of degree modifying 'kind'.

micro_quiz.q: Which is an adverb of frequency?

micro_quiz.explanation: Use the adverb 'well' to modify the verb 'plays'.

challenge.q: Identify the error: 'The students answered very intelligent.'
challenge.explanation: An adverb 'intelligently' is needed to modify the verb 'answered'.

challenge.q: Which sentence places the frequency adverb correctly?
challenge.explanation: Frequency adverbs follow the verb 'be': 'is always busy'.

challenge.q: Choose the correct comparative adverb: 'He works ___ than his brother.'
challenge.explanation: 'hard' is both adjective and adverb; its comparative is 'harder'.
